report.summary: The outlier check identified IQR outliers in two of the three numeric features (feature_x and feature_y), each affecting 1 of 30 rows (3.33%). The correlation check found a perfect Pearson correlation of 1.0 between feature_x and feature_y, exceeding the 0.95 threshold. Thus, the numeric features contain both isolated extreme values and a strong linear relationship that may indicate redundancy or leakage. No outliers were found in feature_z and no other high correlations were detected.

interpretation.text: The single outlier in feature_x (value outside [-13.5, 44.5]) could be a data entry error, measurement anomaly, or a legitimate extreme; with only 30 rows, its impact on some models may be disproportionate.
Similarly, the outlier in feature_y (outside [-26, 90]) warrants domain review before any automatic capping or removal.

A Pearson correlation of 1.0 between feature_x and feature_y indicates they move together perfectly, suggesting they may be duplicate measurements or derived from each other; retaining both could cause multicollinearity in linear models.
The perfect correlation does not alone prove data leakage, but it raises a flag to examine feature provenance and whether one encodes information about the target.
Only three numeric columns were examined; other columns (if any) were not assessed, limiting the scope of the findings.
Because the dataset contains only 30 rows, percentages like 3.33% outlier rate and a correlation >=0.95 may be less reliable; results should be interpreted with caution.

next_steps: Review the specific rows flagged as outliers in feature_x and feature_y with domain experts.
Consider applying robust scaling or transformation to mitigate the effect of the identified outliers.
Evaluate whether to drop or combine feature_x and feature_y due to their perfect correlation.
Compute additional correlation metrics (e.g., Spearman) and assess multicollinearity diagnostics.
Document the provenance of feature_x and feature_y to rule out leakage.
If more numeric features exist, run outlier and correlation checks on them.
